title: Greenfield-to-Brownfield VPC Migration & Onboarding Playbook (draft)
content:
Purpose and scope:

This is a working playbook for migrating customers from an existing (brownfield) corporate network into a Redwood Private VPC or for onboarding customers who are expanding from a small greenfield pilot into a full production VPC. The doc focuses on the intersection of network design, Terraform module migration/compatibility, and safe cutover plans. Goal is an operationally repeatable path that minimizes customer downtime and avoids IP overlap/route conflicts.

Audience:
- Solutions Eng / Customer Network Engineers
- Private Deployments SREs and Platform Engineers
- Customer Security/Network Teams

High-level migration patterns (summary):
1) Lift-and-extend (preferred for minimal infra change): create a dedicated Redwood VPC alongside customer networks and peer via transit or direct connect; advertise specific prefixes with BGP.
2) Routed overlay (short-term): use NATing and prefix translation to avoid overlap; useful for quick pilot ramp but not long-term.
3) Re-IP / remap (last resort): coordinate re-addressing with customer apps; high-friction but removes overlap permanently.

Pre-engagement checklist (customer readiness):
- Confirm primary contact + alternate contact, escalation path.
- Obtain current network diagram (subnet CIDRs, NAT gateways, on-prem edge IPs, firewall rules).
- Confirm IP ownership, RFC1918 usage, and any overlapping ranges across tenant orgs.
- Collect BGP ASN, edge IPs, allowed MTU, and path MTU constraints.
- Confirm required egress destinations and any blocked destinations on customer side.
- KMS/HSM key ownership and rotation requirements for Private control plane.

Discovery & design decisions (templates):
- Model selection: Dedicated VPC (interconnect + BGP) vs Private VPC with VPC peering. Decision driven by SLOs, egress patterns, and compliance.
- Subnet segmentation: control plane, data plane, GPU pools, management VMs, bastion hosts. Use /24 minimum for each functional zone.
- Routing: prefer BGP for deterministic pathing; fallback to static routes for simple pilots.
- Egress architecture: centralized NAT vs per-subnet NAT depending on telemetry/compliance.

Terraform module notes (compatibility + migration tips):
- Module versions: customers on older terraform-private-modules v1.x will have iface naming and route table differences. Always run terraform plan in a sandbox account first.
- Deprecated inputs: module.network.enable_shared_peering (v1.x) was replaced in v2.0 by module.network.peering_profiles[]. Upgrade strategy: add new input with default set to previous value, run plan, and apply in a non-production slice.
- State migration: if importing existing cloud resources into Redwood modules, use terraform import + state mv to the module paths. Document the exact import commands in the engagement ticket.
- Drift mitigation: enable remote state locking and add a pre-apply hook check in CI to compare cloud routes to terraform plan.
- Example caution: changing subnet CIDR in-place will recreate NAT/GW resources — schedule maintenance window.

Upgrade and cutover plan (phases):
Phase 0 — Planning (2–3 weeks):
- Finalize small design doc with customer, obtain approvals, schedule maintenance windows.
- Create separate Terraform workspace for migration.
- Run automated pre-check scripts (IP overlap checker, BGP reachability test).

Phase 1 — Staging build (1 week):
- Provision staging VPC using Redwood modules, mirror customer route tables and firewall policies.
- Validate routing with synthetic traffic and tcpdump on edge instances.
- Share staging test results with customer (latency, egress path, packet loss).

Phase 2 — Partial cutover (weekend, 4–8 hours):
- Establish BGP session, advertise a narrow set of prefixes (non-production).
- Move a small service or single subnet to Redwood VPC and validate.
- Run rollback drill: withdraw prefixes and ensure traffic reflows to customer on-prem.

Phase 3 — Full cutover (longer window, 8–24 hours):
- Schedule DNS TTL reduction beforehand.
- Advertise full set of production prefixes, monitor route convergence.
- Disable legacy NAT paths only after verifying telemetry for 30–60 minutes.

Rollback criteria (automated + manual):
- Packet loss > 1% sustained for 5 minutes to critical services.
- TCP connection failure rate spike > 3x baseline for 10 minutes.
- BGP flap or route leak detected (manual or automated alarms).
- If rollback triggered: withdraw Redwood prefixes, restore customer edge advertisement, and revert Terraform workspace to previous state + re-apply.

Operational runbook snippets (day-of):
- Step A: Confirm contact list and access to customer edge console.
- Step B: Record BGP sessions and route tables (pre-cutover snapshot).
- Step C: Bring up BGP with local-preference lower for test prefixes and then increase once stable.
- Step D: Validate egress IPs using curl to public headers and check NAT IP match.

Security & compliance notes:
- Audit logs: ensure flow logs are enabled for all subnets containing customer data.
- KMS access: share key policies and restrict to customer admin principal where required.
- PCI/HIPAA: note that ZTA (zero trust) firewalls and per-subnet inspection are typically required — add to design if requested.

Validation checklist (post-cutover):
- Application health checks green for 24 hours.
- Telemetry: latency, p95 token-serving times within SLOs.
- Billing: unexpected egress costs within forecast +/- 15%.
- Security: no unexpected open ports from Redwood VPC to public networks.

Common gotchas we've observed (lessons learned):
- Overlapping management ranges: customers often use 10.0.0.0/8 in several departments which leads to opaque routing behaviors. Prefer: recommend unique /16 per customer org in onboarding.
- MTU mismatches: containers and GPU nodes sometimes hit PMTU issues when traversing VPNs; test with ICMP path MTU.
- Terraform zero-downtime patterns: avoid changing subnets or nat gateway attachments in-place unless split-rollout is planned.

Communication templates (to be adapted):
- Pre-cutover email subject: [Action required] Redwood VPC cutover window for <customer> — please confirm contacts and maintenance approval
- Post-cutover summary: short bullet list with success indicators and links to dashboards, rollback audit, and cost estimates.

Open action items (owner & ETA):
- Jordan: finalize staging test harness and add automations for BGP flapping detection (ETA 2025-03-12).
- Sofia: update terraform module README with import examples and state migration checklist (ETA 2025-03-19).
- Priya: draft customer-facing maintenance email template (ETA 2025-03-07).

Appendix A — quick Terraform commands (operational notes, not full snippets):
- terraform workspace new <customer>-migration-staging
- terraform import module.network.aws_vpc.main vpc-0123456789
- terraform state mv aws_route_table.old_path module.network.aws_route_table.main
- Run plan and manual review before apply: terraform plan -var-file=secrets.tfvars | tee plan.out

Appendix B — validation scripts and links:
- IP overlap checker: internal tool link in linked_artifacts.
- BGP simulator: run synthetic advertisement tests to ensure route acceptance.

Notes and unresolved questions (for next iteration):
- Determine a standard minimum MTU baseline for customer tunnels.
- Formalize policy for when to require re-IP vs NAT overlay.
- Add automated Terraform guardians to detect destructive plan actions and require human approval on PRs.

This is a draft. Expect iterative updates as we execute a few migrations and capture exact timings and failure modes. If you run into an edge-case not covered here, add a short incident note to the engagement ticket and append a short summary to this doc so the playbook can be continuously improved.
